item.title: Breakfast Wrap: Parliament in solidarity with Helen Haines
item.description:
Federal parliament will sit today for the first time since independent MP Dr. Helen Haines was attacked outside her electorate office.

Parliamentary business will be suspended, with the prime minister to move a motion expressing support for Ms Haines and her family.

She remains in hospital in a serious but stable condition.

Then - Brazilians have been voting in a hugely consequential election that could take the country down two very different paths. We cross to Sao Paulo as polls close.

item.title: Breakfast Wrap: The $25b energy project causing a political headache
item.description:
A major review into Australia's biggest renewable energy project has found Snowy Hydro 2.0 could cost up to $25 billion, with the completion date pushed out another year.

The project had an initial budget of $2-billion dollars and was originally expected to start operating in 2021.

It's now it's expected to not be fully operational until 2029. 

We hear from the government, the opposition and the project's CEO. 

Then, 12 months ago we spoke to Dr Saya Aziz - an Australian anaesthetist working in Gaza, who described horrific scenes of mass casualties, medical equipment shortages, even a lack of soap - along with the constant fear of air strikes. She comes back on the show after returning from her second trip to Gaza.

item.title: Breakfast Wrap: Why are house prices falling?
item.description:
House prices have fallen in all capital cities for the first time in 15 years - that's according to new data from listings company Domain.

Prices across the capitals fell 4.7% in the September quarter - wiping almost $60,000 off the median price of a home.

We hear from the Federal Housing Minister Claire O'Neill. 

Then, we'll turn to the Greens,  and party leader David Shoebridge's message on our show that he expects Jordon Steele-John to take leave from the party.

item.title: Breakfast Wrap: How can we better protect politicians?
item.description:
Politicians are raising security fears of their own, in the wake of an attack on prominent independent MP Dr helen Haines.

So how can we better protect the people representing us?

Then, One Nation leader Senator Pauline Hanson apologises for a cartoon mocking Senator Jacqui Lambie's health struggles after she suffers vaginal prolapse.

You'll hear from One Nation deputy leader Barnaby Joyce.

And we''ll also cross to Canada to find out about an effort to split the country.

item.title: Breakfast Wrap: Australia rocked by attack on Dr Helen Haines
item.description:
How are representatives across the political spectrum digesting news of an attack on an Australian politician?

Today's episode of the Breakfast Wrap hears from the bystander who intervened in Wangaratta, the town's Mayor, as well as independent federal politicians, the government and the opposition, the House Speaker and historical context from Michelle Grattan.

item.title: Breakfast Wrap: Thousands arrested in French unrest
item.description:
Thousands of pepole have been arrested across France following days of chaotic unrest.

We'll take you to the streets of Paris and we'll hear how the French President is responding.

Then, where is the line for political satire? 

Independent Senator Jacqui Lambie thinks One Nation has  crossed it, with its latest video that mocks her health battle after she publicly revealed that she suffered vaginal prolapse.

item.title: Breakfast Wrap: Intergenerational Report's focus on who we are and where we're going
item.description: Is Australia prepared for the challenges in the decades ahead for the nation? The federal government has just released the latest Intergenerational Report which shows how an aging population is expected to reshape the economy in the next 40 years. The report predicts that for the first time, deaths will outpace births in Australia by the mid 2060s. As the number of tax-paying Australians potential shrinks, the next four decades will see successive budget deficits. This comes as a Senate Inquiry has delivered 11 recommendations in the wake of last year's massive Optus Triple-Zero outage, which has been linked to two deaths.
